subject: Post-call: model fit & next steps / quality regression concern
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jenny Lee <jenny.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + recommended models / prompt sets

Hi Jenny — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- What we heard: Acme wants a concise product-summary generator with strict length limits and high factuality for product pages (primarily US catalog, ~5k SKUs). Latency target: <300ms p95 for prod endpoints.
- Recommended starting models: redwood-m-2 (balanced latency/cost), redwood-l-1 (higher quality for tricky SKUs).
- Immediate ask from you: share a small prompt set and a few representative SKUs so we can run a focused eval.

Attached: prompt_sets_acme_v1.csv (30 sample prompts) and benchmark_summary_20261005.pdf (baseline numbers vs. our recommendations).

Next steps we propose:
1) You validate the sample prompts (Jenny) — reply with any edits or a couple of failing examples by Wed 10/7.
2) We'll run a model-fit eval across redwood-m-2 and redwood-l-1 and share per-prompt diffs + quality scores by EOD 10/7.
3) If you see anything concerning, we can pin your production endpoint to a specific model version while we investigate regressions.

If anything is missing from my summary, let me know.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: prompt_sets_acme_v1.csv, benchmark_summary_20261005.pdf

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. A couple of quick notes from our side: 

- We ran the sample prompts against our internal prod endpoint earlier this morning and noticed a drop in product summary quality after the platform update that rolled model redwood-m-2 -> redwood-m-3.0 last week. Several summaries are now missing key spec lines and hallucinating attributes.
- I attached a short CSV with the 6 failing examples we saw (I'll upload to the SFTP if you prefer).

Can you flag if you see the same behavior on your side? If this is tied to the recent model variant update, we might need to pin or rollback while you investigate — we can't tolerate a production-quality drop while we're validating.

-jenny
Jenny Lee
Senior PM, AI Platform | Acme Retail

Vivek — looping you in from the engineering side. Jenny found clear regressions after the redwood-m-3.0 rollout; she attached 6 failing prompts. Can you: 

- Confirm whether the platform rollout included a model binary change (v2.9 -> v3.0) or a config/kernel change.
- Advise on short-term mitigation (pin to v2.9, staged rollback, dedicated endpoint).
- Tell us how long an incident pin would take to apply and whether there are cost/latency tradeoffs.

Jenny — Vivek is our runtime lead and will own the technical assessment. Vivek, I also attached our internal benchmark_summary_20261005.pdf and prompt sets.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jenny Lee <jenny.lee@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + regression examples — can eng advise on rollback/pinning?

Hi Jenny / Marissa — thanks for the heads up and the failing prompts. Quick findings after a first pass: 

- What happened: On 2026-09-29 we promoted the redwood-m-3.0 variant as the default for the m-series family. The change included updated attention kernels and a minor tokenizer normalization tweak. In our canaries we saw small latency wins with comparable metrics on our internal evals, but we missed a small set of content-preservation regressions for tightly constrained templates (your product-summary use case).

- Short-term mitigations available now:
  1) Pin Acme's prod endpoint to redwood-m-2.9 (previous default) — this is the fastest option and preserves your current quality characteristics. We can apply pinning at the route level; it takes ~30 minutes to propagate and requires a brief restart window (no data loss).
  2) Rollback the default to v2.9 globally — longer process (2–4 hours for coordination, dependent on cross-customer impact).
  3) Create a dedicated endpoint backed by v2.9 for Acme — slightly higher cost but isolates you from future family-wide promotions.

- Next steps I recommend:
  - Temporary pin to v2.9 for 72 hours while we run a focused diff eval across your prompt set and our broader regression suite.
  - Engineering will produce a model-diff-v2.9-v3.0.txt with token-level diffs + metric deltas by EOD 10/7.
  - If diffs confirm a regression, we can either keep the pin for longer or apply a targeted rollback for constrained templates.

Ticket: INF-5421 (I've created the investigation ticket and attached initial diffs).

Marissa — if you have customer sign-off we can apply the pin today. Jenny — do you want us to pin now or after you review the first diffs?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Runtime Lead | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachments: model-diff-v2.9-v3.0.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & next steps / quality regression concern

Thanks Vivek — and thanks Jenny for surfacing this so quickly. Jenny: we recommend the following path to minimize disruption while we validate: 

1) We'll pin your production route to redwood-m-2.9 now (30-minute propagation).
2) Engineering will run the full diff eval across your prompt set + 1k additional prompts from your catalog and post results to INF-5421 by EOD 10/07.
3) If engineering confirms a regression we will keep the pin and schedule a planned rollback for the affected templates; if not, we will unpin and monitor for 48 hours.

Please reply with a quick OK and we'll apply the pin immediately.

Best,
Marissa
